summary: Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, later holding posts at Bonn (1974–2004) and Goethe University Frankfurt.
Rudolf Lange was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1874–1881) and the University of Berlin (~1887–1920).
Rudolf Much was a specialist in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1882–1887) and served on its faculty from circa 1895 to 1934.

Rudolf Otto worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and under Richard von Garbe, later holding posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig and under Heinrich Zimmer. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), University of Freiburg (~1887–1913), and University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift, with Heinrich Ewald, and with Eugène Burnouf. He spent his career at the University of Tübingen as a lecturer in 1845 and Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

Rudrapatna Shamasastry specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. He earned degrees from Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta, later serving as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, Curator at ORI Mysore, and Director of Mysore Archaeological Department.

Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen studied at Leiden University under supervisors Jens-Uwe Hartmann and Paul Harrison, among other teachers, and holds a post at the University of Heidelberg.

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), later serving on the faculty of Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. His career includes posts at the University of Bristol and as President of the Pali Text Society (2003).

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who was educated at Nagoya University. Her career includes research posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 1998, 2015) and the Eastern Institute (attested 2015).

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. She studied at the University of Chicago and under teachers including D. T. Suzuki and Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki, later heading the Buddhist Society of America and First Zen Institute in Kyoto.

Ruth Gamble is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman, later holding posts at ANU and the University of Munich.

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Princeton University, studied under Jinbo Shi, and served as Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.
Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Acadia University and earned a PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under the supervision of Jason Neelis.

Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a researcher in Buddhist and religious studies who earned a Master of Arts in Religious Studies at Naropa University, where he studied under Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, and several other academic and traditional teachers.

Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Brown and Harvard, and held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley, and Wesleyan University.
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held academic posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2015–2020) and as a lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Berlin. He lectured at the University of Berlin (~1936–1938) and served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1953–1980).
Ryoichi Kondo was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).
